meta.status: PLACEHOLDER starter bank — exam-prep expansion comes in later waves; Mike Holt to check every question

questions.q: What is the maximum breaker size for a 12 AWG copper conductor on a general branch circuit?
Along a dwelling wall line, receptacles must be spaced so no point is more than how far from a receptacle?
questions.why: 210.52(A): no point more than 6 ft from a receptacle (12 ft max between receptacles).

questions.q: How deep must the working space be in front of a 120/240V residential panel?
questions.why: 110.26 / Table 110.26(A)(1): 3 ft for 0–150V to ground, condition 1.

questions.q: How are equipment grounding conductors counted for box fill?
choices: One volume allowance for all of them together
questions.why: 314.16(B)(5): all EGCs in the box count as a single volume allowance based on the largest EGC.

questions.q: A 48A continuous EV charger needs what minimum branch-circuit rating?
What is the maximum conduit fill for three or more conductors?
In a subpanel (separate from the service), grounds and neutrals must be:
questions.why: The neutral-to-ground bond happens at the service only (250.24 / 250.142(B)).

questions.q: Bathroom receptacles require a circuit of what rating?
questions.why: 210.11(C)(3): at least one 20A circuit for bathroom receptacles.

questions.q: For AC equipment, conductor size is chosen from the nameplate value called:
questions.why: Article 440: conductors per nameplate MCA; breaker/fuse per nameplate max (MOCP).

questions.q: How many 20A small-appliance branch circuits does a kitchen need at minimum?
A receptacle must be installed within how many feet of a bathroom basin's outside edge?
questions.why: 210.52(D): within 3 ft of the outside edge of each basin.

questions.q: The 120% rule for backfed solar breakers applies to:
questions.why: 705.12(B)(3)(2): the busbar may be loaded to 120% of its rating by the SUM of 125% of the power-source output current PLUS the rating of the overcurrent device protecting the busbar — and that backfed breaker sits at the opposite end of the busbar from the main, with a do-not-relocate warning label. (A separate method, (B)(3)(3), caps the sum of ALL breaker ratings feeding the busbar at the busbar rating itself.)
